claim: AC-1 gravity exemption: the ptero flight loads the FLYXP X-velocity table and the load-bearing comment states "NO GRAVITY!" — the ptero obeys no gravity pair (JOUSTRV4.SRC:1506).

source.verbatim: LDX	#FLYXP		ADD IN BUMPX,Y; AND VELX,Y; NO GRAVITY!

claim: AC-1: the ptero integrates its position by calling ADDGRX, the entry ONE instruction past the mount ADDB GRAV, so the gravity add is skipped (JOUSTRV4.SRC:1508).
AC-1: ADDGRA — the MOUNT entry — ADDs the variable gravity to VY every frame; the ptero starts after it (JOUSTRV4.SRC:6489).

source.verbatim: ADDGRA	ADDB	GRAV		ADD IN VARIABLE GRAVITY

claim: AC-1: ADDGRX begins at the position integrate (ADDD PPOSY+1,U, the fractional distance), one instruction past the gravity add — the ptero enters here (JOUSTRV4.SRC:6494).

source.verbatim: ADDGRX	ADDD	PPOSY+1,U	ADD IN FRACTIONAL DISTANCE

claim: AC-1: the FLYXP ptero X-velocity ladder low endpoint is -$0300 (index −8), wider than the mount FLYX -$0200 (JOUSTRV4.SRC:1587).
AC-1: the FLYXP label sits on the ZERO entry ($0000) in the MIDDLE of the nine-rung ladder — the FLYX house convention (JOUSTRV4.SRC:1591).
AC-1: the FLYXP ptero X-velocity ladder high endpoint is $0300 (index +8) = 768 decimal — the ptero tops out wider than the mount $0200 (JOUSTRV4.SRC:1595).
AC-2 lance offset: B starts from the player LANTZ (LDB PLANTZ,U) — a skidding player (PLANTZ 2) lowers the lance and shifts the band (JOUSTRV4.SRC:4971).

source.verbatim: LDB	PLANTZ,U	LANTZ ON CORRECT LINE?

claim: AC-2 lance offset: ADDB PPOSY+1,U adds the player WHOLE-pixel Y (offset +1 is the pixel byte, fraction excluded) (JOUSTRV4.SRC:4972).
AC-2 lance offset: SUBB PPOSY+1,X subtracts the ptero WHOLE-pixel Y, so B = PLANTZ + playerPixelY − pteroPixelY (JOUSTRV4.SRC:4973).
AC-2 band select: CMPA #FLY2-FLY1 tests the ptero PIMAGE against the frame stride 12 — "ATTACKING FRAME?" — selecting the 8±3 band over 10±2 (JOUSTRV4.SRC:4975).
AC-2 band select: BLS 13$ branches to the wings-down/glide band (10±2) when the ptero is NOT in the attacking frame (JOUSTRV4.SRC:4976).
AC-2 frame stride: FLY1 is an RMB 12 buffer, so FLY2-FLY1 = 12, the attacking-frame discriminant threshold (JOUSTRV4.SRC:140).
AC-2 frame stride: FLY3 is the third consecutive RMB 12 buffer, so FLY3-FLY1 = 24 — the attacking frame is PIMAGE > 12 (JOUSTRV4.SRC:142).
AC-2 attacking band: SUBB #15-7 fudges the lance offset to the centre of the pterodactyl mouth at 8 (JOUSTRV4.SRC:4978).

source.verbatim: SUBB	#15-7		FUDGE FROM LANTZ TO CENTER OF PTERO-MOUTH

claim: AC-2 attacking band: CMPB #3 — "WITHIN 7 PIXELS?" — kills only when |offset − 8| ≤ 3 (JOUSTRV4.SRC:4981).
AC-2 glide band: SUBB #15-5 fudges the lance offset to the centre of the pterodactyl mouth at 10 for the wings-up frames (JOUSTRV4.SRC:4986).

source.verbatim: SUBB	#15-5		FUDGE FROM LANTZ TO CENTER OF PTERO-MOUTH

claim: AC-2 glide band: CMPB #2 — "WITHIN 5 PIXELS?" — kills only when |offset − 10| ≤ 2 (JOUSTRV4.SRC:4989).
AC-2 band fail: BHI OSTBO drops an out-of-band lance into the NORMAL joust — "CANNOT KILL PTERODACTYL" (JOUSTRV4.SRC:4990).

source.verbatim: 14$	BHI	OSTBO		 BR=NO, CANNOT KILL PTERODACTYL

claim: AC-2 opposite facings: LDA PFACE,U reads the player facing — "FACING IN OPPSITE DIRECTIONS?" — for the EOR test against the ptero PFACE (JOUSTRV4.SRC:4991).

source.verbatim: LDA	PFACE,U		FACING IN OPPSITE DIRECTIONS?

claim: AC-2 opposite facings: BPL OSTBO — same-sign facings EOR to a non-negative byte and CANNOT KILL the pterodactyl (JOUSTRV4.SRC:4993).

source.verbatim: BPL	OSTBO		 BR=NO, CANNOT KILL PTERODACTYL

claim: AC-2 facing-into: LDD COLDX (ptero.x − player.x) — "FACING PTERODACTYL?" — decides which side the ptero is on (JOUSTRV4.SRC:4994).
AC-2 facing-into: BPL 11$ — with the ptero on the right and the player facing right (into it), the pterodactyl is KILLED (JOUSTRV4.SRC:5001).
AC-2 fallback: OSTBO is the ordinary joust (LDB PLANTZ,U, the plantHeight compare) any kill-window miss falls into — the epic rules the ptero wins it (JOUSTRV4.SRC:5002).
AC-2 score chain: P7DEC (the ptero enemy) decodes its DVALUE through SCRHUN — the 4th FDB operand names the DVALUR routine (JOUSTRV4.SRC:5575).
AC-2 score (DERIVED): the ptero DVALUE byte is $10 (2nd FCB operand of P7DEC); through SCRHUN this is 1 thousand + 0 hundreds = 1000, verified in emulation (JOUSTRV4.SRC:5577).
AC-2 score chain: SCRHUN is the "INCREMENT SCORE BY THOUSANDS AND HUNDREDS" routine — the high nibble is thousands, the low nibble hundreds (JOUSTRV4.SRC:7340).

source.verbatim: *	INCREMENT SCORE BY THOUSANDS AND HUNDREDS

claim: AC-2 score chain: SCRHUN LDY DSCORE,X points at the score area before adding the BCD thousands/hundreds digit (JOUSTRV4.SRC:7346).

source.verbatim: SCRHUN	LDY	DSCORE,X	GET SCORE AREA

claim: AC-2 score chain: SCRHUN ADDA 2,Y adds the DVALUE byte at the score THOUSANDS/HUNDREDS position, so $10 = 1000 (JOUSTRV4.SRC:7348).
AC-3 dispatch: WJSRTB is the six-entry wave subroutine table; entry 0 is the NOP routine WAVRTS (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2586).
AC-3 dispatch: WPTERO is the SIXTH WJSRTB entry (index 5) — the PTERODACTYL WAVE, which jt2-5 routes as WAVE_TYPES[5] = ptero (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2591).
AC-3 spawn count: WPTEN is the wave-row byte "NBR OF PTERODACTYLS IN THIS WAVE" — the ptero nibble the spawn count reads (JOUSTRV4.SRC:179).

source.verbatim: WPTEN	RMB	1	NBR OF PTERODACTYLS IN THIS WAVE

claim: AC-3 spawn count: the ptero wave routine reads LDA WPTEN,X to get the number of pterodactyls for this wave (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2614).

source.verbatim: LDA	WPTEN,X		 GET NBR OF PTERODCTYLS FOR THIS WAVE

claim: AC-3 spawn count: STA PJOYT,Y stores WPTEN as the NUMBER OF PTERODACTYLS TO CREATE for the wave (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2615).

source.verbatim: STA	PJOYT,Y		NUMBER OF PTERODACTYLS TO CREATE
